memo:
### Position read
Opponent advanced to center (3,3). We answered with a piece from (4,7) to (4,4). Losses remain 0 for every color; no eliminations. Initial edge formations otherwise remain intact, with the opponent's top-edge gap at (0,3) and our right-edge gap at (4,7).

### Our plan
Defend (4,4), contest (4,3), and develop same-color flank geometry near the center. Avoid occupying (3,4) while the opponent can flank it using (3,3) plus a top-edge piece landing at (3,5). Seek supported center occupation rather than isolated intrusions.

### Opponent tendencies
The opening move immediately claimed (3,3), signaling a center-first approach.

### Lessons
Before each move, test every exposed piece for a one-move same-color sandwich by either opposing color. A piece may safely move into a sandwich, but cannot safely remain where the opponent can complete one.

### Position read
Center is split: opponent pieces at (3,3) and (4,3), our Blue at (4,4), with (3,4) empty. Losses are all 0. Green moved (1,0)->(1,5), blocking Red's column-5 route to (4,5), which otherwise sandwiched Blue (4,4) and the opponent's (4,3) against Red (3,3).

### Our plan
On Blue's turn, reassess the center after Red moves. Blue (4,4) remains vulnerable to a Yellow landing at (4,5), using Yellow (4,3) as the far flank, so evacuate or tactically alter that line before Yellow acts. Contest (3,4)/(4,3) only with support and build same-color Blue or Green flank pairs.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent has claimed (3,3) and (4,3) immediately, showing an aggressive center-first plan. Their adjacent center pieces also create mixed-color sandwich geometry that can expose both teams.

### Lessons
Scan beyond every exposed piece for a same-color far flank and a legal landing at the opposite end. Blocking an attacker's travel lane can be the only defense when the threatened color is not acting.

### Position read
The opponent holds three center squares: Red at (3,3),(3,4) and Yellow at (4,3); our Blue at (4,4) denies the immediate center win. Losses remain 0. Blue moved (5,7)->(5,5), blocking Yellow (7,5)'s vertical route to (4,5), which would have sandwiched Blue (4,4) against Yellow (4,3). Green at (1,5) also blocks Red access down column 5.

### Our plan
Preserve or replace the blocker at (4,4) while attacking the opponent's central trio. On Green's turn, look for a safe move toward (3,5), (4,5), or supporting lanes that cannot friendly-fire Blue. Build same-color flank geometry; the immediate strategic target is Yellow (4,3) or either central Red.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent is aggressively center-first and will seek a landing at (4,5) to clear our blocker, or rearrange the central pieces to create another capture lane. Expect Yellow to challenge column 5 or vacate (4,3) tactically.

### Lessons
When a center blocker cannot evacuate because the opponent would win instantly, defend it by blocking the attacker's travel route. Recheck alternate attackers and empty gaps before assuming a sandwich exists.

### Position read
The opponent still occupies three center squares: Red at (3,3),(3,4) and Yellow at (4,3); our Blue at (4,4) prevents the center win. Yellow advanced to (4,6), threatening to land at (4,5) and sandwich Blue against Yellow (4,3). Green moved (1,5)->(4,5), occupying that critical landing square. Losses remain 0.

### Our plan
Keep at least one of our pieces on the center while dismantling the opponent's central trio. Green at (4,5) protects the immediate geometry and Blue at (5,5) provides nearby reinforcement. On Blue's turn, first verify whether Red created a new capture against (4,4) or (4,5); otherwise seek a safe attack on Yellow (4,3) or Red (3,4).

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent is center-first and used Yellow (4,6) to prepare a direct sandwich of our blocker. Expect Red to open another landing lane, attack Green (4,5), or alter the central formation so Yellow can capture from a different direction.

### Lessons
A threatened center blocker can be defended by occupying the attacker's required landing square. Recheck all four rook lines after every opponent move because only a same-color far flank completes a sandwich.

### Position read
The opponent holds Red at (3,3),(3,4) and Yellow at (4,3), while our Blue at (4,4) blocks the center win. Green (4,5) blocks Yellow (4,6)->(4,5), which would sandwich the center Blue against Yellow (4,3). Blue moved (1,7)->(1,4); losses are all 0.

### Our plan
Blue now threatens (1,4)->(2,4), capturing Red (3,4) against Blue (4,4). Preserve Blue (4,4), Green (4,5), and preferably Blue (5,5), since together they deny Yellow's direct attack lanes. On Green's turn, reinforce without vacating (4,5) unless the Yellow flank at (4,6) has been removed.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent is center-first. Expect Yellow to create interference around column 4, then Red to move (3,4), occupy (2,4), or otherwise break Blue's staged sandwich.

### Lessons
Use a center holder as the stationary far flank for a forcing capture threat. Green (4,5) is tactically essential because vacating it permits Yellow (4,6)->(4,5) to capture Blue (4,4).

### Position read
The opponent holds Red (3,3),(3,4) and Yellow (4,3); our Blue (4,4) denies the center win. Green (4,5) must remain: vacating it lets Yellow (4,6)->(4,5) capture both Blue (4,4) against Yellow (4,3) and Blue (5,5) against Yellow (6,5). Green moved (5,0)->(5,4), also blocking Yellow (7,4)'s vertical route. Losses remain 0.

### Our plan
Blue still threatens (1,4)->(2,4), capturing Red (3,4) against Blue (4,4). If Red evacuates (3,4), consider Blue occupying that center square. Preserve Green (4,5), Blue (4,4), and watch the new Green (5,4). Use the central formation to transition from denial into occupation.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent remains center-first and used Yellow (6,5) to create a double-sandwich geometry around Green (4,5). Expect Red to move (3,4) or disrupt the Blue column before the staged capture.

### Lessons
Do not vacate a blocker without scanning every direction from the opponent's newly available landing square. Mixed-color lines can make one landing capture several of our pieces.

### Position read
The opponent holds three center squares: Red (3,3),(3,4) and Yellow (4,3); Blue (4,4) denies victory. Red's new (2,4) threatened Blue (1,4), using Red (0,4)-side landing geometry, so Blue sidestepped to (1,3). Green (4,5) still blocks Yellow (4,6)->(4,5), which would capture Blue (4,4) against Yellow (4,3) and Blue (5,5) against Yellow (6,5). Losses are 0.

### Our plan
Blue now threatens to return (1,3)->(1,4), sandwiching Red (2,4),(3,4) against Blue (4,4) for a double capture. Preserve Blue (4,4), Green (4,5), and Green (5,4). If Red evacuates the column-4 chain, exploit the weakened center and seek occupation of (3,4).

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent is center-first and has responded to our capture setup by inserting Red (2,4), creating both a blockade and a threat against the former Blue position. Expect Red to evacuate one column-4 piece or disrupt the far Blue flank before our return.

### Lessons
Temporary sidesteps can preserve a sandwich threat: capture checks occur on landing, so vacating and later returning to a flank square can trigger the line.

### Position read
The opponent occupies three center squares: Red (3,3),(3,4) and Yellow (4,3); Blue (4,4) prevents the immediate win. Green moved (4,5)->(3,5), escaping Yellow's threatened return to (4,6), which would have captured Green (4,5) and Blue (4,4) against Yellow (4,3). Losses remain 0.

### Our plan
Green (3,5) is now a far flank: Green (3,0)->(3,2) would sandwich both Reds at (3,3),(3,4). Blue also retains the potential (1,3)->(1,4) vertical attack on Reds (2,4),(3,4) against Blue (4,4). Expect Red to vacate or break the shared (3,4) link; then contest the newly opened center while preserving Blue (4,4) and Green (5,4).

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent is center-first. Yellow withdrew from (4,6) to (3,6), preserving mobility and forcing us to address a possible return sandwich.

### Lessons
When one piece anchors several enemy capture lines, relocate it to safety while preserving a new same-color flank. Empty gaps break sandwiches, so verify the entire line before relying on a threat.

### Position read
The opponent still holds three center squares, with Blue (4,4) preventing victory. Green threatens (3,0)->(3,2), sandwiching Reds (3,3),(3,4) against Green (3,5). Yellow can interpose at (3,2), but Green then lands (3,1) and captures Yellow plus both Reds; Yellow (7,1)->(3,1) is the effective blockade.

### Our plan
Blue (1,4) now threatens (1,4)->(2,4), capturing Red (3,4) against Blue (4,4). If that Red retreats to (2,4), Blue (4,4)->(3,4) captures it against Blue (1,4). On Green’s turn, take the double-Red sandwich unless Yellow occupies (3,1). If blocked there, preserve Blue’s trap and improve Green’s center support. Keep Blue (4,4) occupied unless moving it captures the retreating Red.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent prioritizes center occupation and uses Yellow mobility to interfere with capture lanes. Expect Yellow (7,1)->(3,1) to stop Green’s immediate sandwich, followed by a Red attempt to escape or obstruct Blue’s trap.

### Lessons
A threatened piece’s forced retreat square can itself be trapped by relocating the original far flank. Interposed pieces join a sandwich line unless they occupy and block the mover’s route.

### Position read
Green (3,0)->(3,2) captured Reds at (3,3) and (3,4) against Green (3,5), raising Red to 2 losses. The center is now empty at (3,3),(3,4), with Yellow at (4,3) and Blue at (4,4). Red has four pieces remaining: (0,1),(0,2),(0,5),(2,6).

### Our plan
Any further Red capture eliminates that color, so prioritize a safe one-piece capture setup. Keep Blue (4,4) secure to deny the opponent center victory, while Blue (1,4) and Green’s rank-three pair pressure central entry lanes. Look for a same-color flank around Red (2,6), currently beside Blue (2,7), by landing Blue at (2,5).

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent favors center occupation and interference with prepared sandwiches. Expect Red to seek safety or enter an open center square, then Yellow to reinforce (4,3) and challenge Blue (4,4).

### Lessons
When an interposition does not occupy the mover’s route, execute the multi-capture immediately. At 2 losses, every exposed remaining piece of that color is an elimination target.

### Position read
Red has 2 losses and four pieces at (0,1),(0,2),(0,5),(2,3); one more Red capture eliminates it. Blue moved (4,4)->(3,4) because Yellow threatened (4,6)->(4,5), which would sandwich Blue against Yellow (4,3). Center now has Blue (3,4), Yellow (4,3), with (3,3),(4,4) empty.

### Our plan
Keep Blue (3,4) secure and deny the opponent all four center squares. Seek a same-color sandwich on any Red, especially (2,3). Blue (1,4) offers useful vertical support, while Green (3,2) and (3,5) control the third rank. Preserve pieces and avoid allowing Yellow to build flanks around our center occupant.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent prioritizes central occupation and disrupts capture formations. Yellow has an active horizontal pair at (4,3),(4,6), so scan every Blue or Green placed between them. Red will likely move its exposed (2,3) piece or use it to contest the center.

### Lessons
Always check the next color’s one-move sandwich before pursuing an attack. A center foothold is valuable only when it cannot be removed immediately.

### Position read
The opponent holds (4,3) and (4,4), while our Blue holds (3,4). Our Green has moved from (3,5) to (4,5), placing a same-color flank immediately beside the Yellow pair. Red remains one loss from elimination, with pieces at (0,1),(0,2),(0,5),(2,3).

### Our plan
Threaten Green (3,2)->(4,2), which sandwiches both Yellow center pieces against Green (4,5). If Yellow splits the pair, exploit the resulting center vacancy or capture the remaining piece with alternate Green geometry. Keep Blue (3,4) secure and look for any same-color sandwich on Red (2,3).

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent prioritizes central occupation and will likely move one Yellow from row 4 to evade the threatened double capture. Red may use (2,3) to occupy (3,3), forming three opponent-held center squares around our Blue blocker.

### Lessons
Build same-color flanks while checking whether the staging piece can itself be sandwiched. Forcing a central pair to split can be as valuable as an immediate capture.

### Position read
The opponent holds Yellow at (4,3),(4,4), threatened by Green (3,2)->(4,2) against our Green flank at (4,5). Blue has now staged at (7,7), threatening (7,5) to sandwich Yellow (6,5) against Blue (5,5). Red has 2 losses and four pieces remaining.

### Our plan
Exploit the fork: if Yellow leaves the center pair intact, take the Green double capture. If Yellow moves (4,3) and breaks the pair, preserve the Green formation and on our next Blue turn capture Yellow (6,5) via (7,7)->(7,5). If Yellow instead saves (6,5), remove both central Yellow pieces. Keep Blue (3,4) as the center blocker.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent prioritizes center occupation. Yellow’s piece at (4,4) is currently boxed in, so only (4,3) can split the threatened center pair without a capture changing the position.

### Lessons
Create same-color capture threats against two pieces of the color about to act; one move cannot answer both. Recheck that the stationary far flank remains protected through the intervening turns.

### Position read
Green (4,0)->(4,3) captures Yellow (4,4), giving Yellow 1 loss. We now occupy center squares (3,4) with Blue and (4,3) with Green; Yellow remains at (3,3). Blue at (7,7) still has the protected capture (7,7)->(7,5), sandwiching Yellow (6,5) against Blue (5,5). Red has 2 losses and four pieces.

### Our plan
On the next Blue turn, normally play (7,7)->(7,5) to capture Yellow (6,5), unless an immediate win or urgent defense appears. Then contest (4,4) and seek a supported route to remove Yellow (3,3), while watching for a one-piece capture that eliminates Red.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent prioritizes central occupation and used Yellow (4,3)->(3,3) to break a threatened double capture, conceding the other central piece.

### Lessons
When a fork forces one target to move, collect the surviving target without dismantling the independent threat. Central occupation is strongest when each piece has same-color tactical support nearby.

### Position read
Blue (7,7)->(7,5) sandwiches Yellow (6,5) against Blue (5,5), raising Yellow to 2 losses. We retain Blue at (3,4) and Green at (4,3), while Yellow occupies (3,3) and (4,4) is empty. Red also has 2 losses; Blue has 1 after Red's latest sandwich.

### Our plan
Both opponent colors are one loss from elimination. Seek any safe capture of a normal Yellow or Red piece, prioritizing immediate elimination. Defend our center pair and work toward occupying (4,4) after clearing Yellow (3,3). Check whether Green can create a same-color flank around the central Yellow without friendly fire.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent contests the center actively and exploited a same-color Red flank to capture an exposed Blue. Expect Yellow to protect its last life and disrupt our central formation next.

### Lessons
At two losses, every exposed piece is elimination-critical. Preserve same-color support around central pieces and scan both opponent turns for landing-square sandwich threats before advancing.

### Position read
We now occupy three center squares: Green at (3,3) and (4,3), Blue at (3,4). The last center square, (4,4), is empty, with Blue at (5,4) ready to enter it. Both opponent colors remain at 2 losses; Blue has 1 loss and Green 0.

### Our plan
Unless Red somehow disrupts the center, play Blue (5,4)->(4,4) next turn for immediate center victory. Before executing, verify that (4,4) remains empty and all three held center squares remain occupied by our team. If the threat is stopped, resume hunting any normal Red or Yellow piece for the single capture that eliminates that color.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent contests the center and searches for same-color sandwich tactics. Red must answer our immediate center threat now, likely by trying to capture or dislodge one of our three central pieces.

### Lessons
A three-square center formation is decisive when the fourth square has a direct, protected entry. Always check for immediate victory before pursuing elimination captures.

### Position read
We occupy all four central squares after Blue moves from (5,4) to (4,4), alongside Green at (3,3) and (4,3) and Blue at (3,4). This immediately wins by center occupation.

### Our plan
The game is won; no further plan is required.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent passed with Red despite the immediate center threat.

### Lessons
When all four center squares can be occupied by our team in one legal move, execute it immediately because victory is instantaneous.

### Position read
We hold (3,3), (3,4), and (4,3). The remaining center square (4,4) can be occupied by Blue from (4,7).

### Our plan
Complete center occupation now for the immediate win.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent allowed a direct center-completion opportunity.

### Lessons
Verify the source square’s color directly before submitting a decisive move.

### Position read
We occupy all four center squares after Green moves from (4,5) to (4,4), completing an immediate center victory.

### Our plan
The game is won by center occupation.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent left the final center square reachable by Green.

### Lessons
Verify the acting color and use its direct legal center-completing move.
